title: How a Laser Printer Works in 60 Seconds 🖨️⚡ #shorts
description:
A laser printer draws your page with static electricity. A charged drum is "written" by a laser, plastic toner powder sticks only where the laser touched, the paper picks it up, and hot fuser rollers at around 200°C melt it in place. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#laserprinter #printer #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A laser printer *melts plastic* onto your paper at about *200 degrees*.

steps.label: Drum
steps.text: First, a spinning *drum* gets coated in *static charge*.

steps.label: Laser
steps.text: A *laser* sweeps across it, erasing the charge wherever your *letters* go.

steps.label: Toner
steps.text: *Toner* is a fine powder of pigment and plastic. It sticks only to the *laser-drawn* areas.

steps.label: Transfer
steps.text: The drum rolls the powder onto the *paper*, like an invisible *stamp*.

steps.label: Fuser
steps.text: Hot *fuser rollers* melt the plastic, so the print is *bonded* to the page.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Charge, laser, *melt*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
